items.description: Analyze repository structure and available tooling
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce repo_analysis.md documenting: (1) all files and their purposes, (2) .archivara/concept_evolve.py capabilities (evolve, probe, reframe sub-agents), (3) .archivara/semantic_scholar.py capabilities (search, citations, references, recommend, bibtex), (4) identified gaps needing new code. Minimum 300 words.
items.notes: Produced repo_analysis.md (~780 words). Documented all files, both tool capabilities, and 12 code gaps. Fixed syntax errors in concept_evolve.py. Ran ConceptEvolve evolve, generated 8 concept cards, semantic bridge graph, and introspection. Wrote steering_notes.md with 3 directions.

items.description: Literature review: classical results on Euler bricks and perfect cuboids
items.acceptance_criteria: Use WebSearch and semantic_scholar.py to survey classical results including: Halcke (1719) smallest Euler brick (44,117,240), Saunderson (1740) and Euler parametric families, Leech (1977) systematic searches, Lal-Blundon parametrization, Kraitchik's work. Document findings in literature_review.md with at least 8 classical references. Each reference must include author, year, key contribution.
items.notes: literature_review.md Part I covers 9 classical references: Halcke, Saunderson, Euler, Kraitchik, Lal-Blundon, Leech (2 papers), Dickson, Guy, Spohn.

items.description: Literature review: modern computational searches and recent proof attempts
items.acceptance_criteria: Survey and document: (1) Butler's computational search algorithm and its derivatives, (2) De Grey-Gibbs-Helm elliptic curve approach and perfect plinth analysis (arXiv 2401.06784), (3) Sharipov S3-symmetry approach (arXiv 1504.07161), (4) van Luijk algebraic geometry perspective, (5) recent non-existence claims (Lloyd 2022, Agbanwa 2025, arXiv 2602.00239). Append findings to literature_review.md with at least 8 modern references.
items.notes: literature_review.md Part II covers 14 modern references: Rathbun, Butler, Matson, Korec, van Luijk, Bremner, Sharipov (4 papers), De Grey-Gibbs-Helm, Ramsden-Sharipov, Lloyd, Agbanwa, arXiv 2602.00239, Knill.

items.description: Create and populate sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib in repo root contains at least 12 valid BibTeX entries covering: (1) at least 4 classical papers/books on Euler bricks, (2) at least 4 modern computational search papers, (3) at least 2 algebraic geometry or number theory approaches, (4) at least 2 recent proof attempts or surveys. Each entry must have author, title, year, and URL or DOI where available. Use semantic_scholar.py bibtex command where possible.
items.notes: sources.bib has 26 BibTeX entries: 9 classical, 4 computational search, 8 algebraic/number theory, 5 recent proof attempts/surveys.

items.description: Formalize the Diophantine system and catalog known necessary conditions
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce problem_specification.md containing: (1) the 4 Pythagorean-type equations (a²+b²=d_ab², a²+c²=d_ac², b²+c²=d_bc², a²+b²+c²=d_s²), (2) known modular constraints (divisibility by 4, 16; parity conditions; prime factor constraints on space diagonal), (3) at least 5 known necessary conditions from the literature, (4) the reduction to a single degree-12 Diophantine equation as described by Sharipov, (5) known near-miss examples with their gap measurements.

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve for cross-domain insight generation
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve.py evolve with the perfect cuboid problem description. Save output to results/concept_evolve/. Verify at least 6 concept cards are generated spanning domains such as algebraic geometry, lattice theory, modular forms, combinatorial optimization, and constraint satisfaction. Summarize the top 3 most promising cross-domain insights in problem_specification.md.

items.description: Implement core data structures: Cuboid representation and Pythagorean triple generators
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/cuboid.py with: (1) Cuboid class storing edges (a,b,c), computing face diagonals and space diagonal, (2) is_euler_brick() method returning True iff all face diagonals are integers, (3) is_perfect_cuboid() method returning True iff space diagonal is also integer, (4) Pythagorean triple generator using (m,n) parametrization, (5) at least 10 unit tests in tests/test_cuboid.py all passing. Verify Cuboid(44,117,240).is_euler_brick() == True.

items.description: Implement brute-force Euler brick finder with verification
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/brute_force.py that: (1) systematically searches for Euler bricks up to a given edge bound, (2) for each Euler brick found, checks if space diagonal is integer, (3) uses modular pre-filtering (skip a≡2 mod 4, apply parity constraints) to reduce search space, (4) outputs results as JSON with edges, face diagonals, space diagonal, and gap (how close space diagonal is to integer). Verify it finds at least the 5 smallest known Euler bricks: (44,117,240), (240,252,275), (85,132,720), (140,480,693), (160,231,792).

items.description: Implement comprehensive verification checker for all 7 integer conditions
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/verifier.py with verify_cuboid(a,b,c) function that: (1) computes all 7 values (3 edges, 3 face diagonals, 1 space diagonal), (2) checks each for exact integrality using integer square root, (3) returns a detailed report dict with each value, whether it's integer, and the residual error, (4) includes batch verification mode for checking lists of candidates. Unit tests must verify known Euler bricks pass face diagonal checks and fail space diagonal check.

items.description: Run baseline enumeration and establish performance benchmarks
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute brute_force.py with edge bound 1000 and record: (1) total Euler bricks found (should match known count for that range), (2) wall-clock time, (3) candidates checked vs. candidates surviving modular filters, (4) nearest near-miss perfect cuboid found (smallest fractional part of space diagonal). Save results to results/baseline_benchmarks.json. Document search rate (candidates/second) and filter efficiency (% eliminated by modular constraints).

items.description: Profile baseline implementation and identify computational bottlenecks
items.acceptance_criteria: Profile brute_force.py using cProfile or time measurements. Produce results/profiling_report.md documenting: (1) time breakdown by function, (2) percentage of time in integer square root checks vs. iteration vs. filtering, (3) memory usage, (4) identified bottleneck operations. Establish reference performance: candidates per second at bound=1000, bound=5000, bound=10000. Create a scaling plot (log-log) of runtime vs. bound.

items.description: Implement modular arithmetic sieve for aggressive candidate filtering
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/modular_sieve.py implementing: (1) pre-computation of quadratic residue tables mod p for primes p up to at least 100, (2) combined sieve eliminating (a,b,c) triples where any face diagonal or space diagonal is provably non-integer mod p, (3) multi-prime sieve combining constraints from at least 10 primes. Demonstrate at least 95% candidate elimination rate compared to brute force. Benchmark shows >= 5x speedup over baseline brute_force.py at bound=5000.

items.description: Implement parametric family generators for Euler brick families
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/parametric.py implementing at least 3 known parametric families: (1) Saunderson's family, (2) Euler's two-parameter family, (3) at least one modern family from the literature (e.g., from Bremner 1988 or Piezas collection). For each family, generate at least 100 Euler bricks and check each for perfect cuboid property. Document which families produce the closest near-misses (smallest fractional part of space diagonal).

items.description: Implement near-miss scoring and statistical analysis system
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/near_miss.py that: (1) defines a near-miss score as min(fractional_part(space_diagonal), 1-fractional_part(space_diagonal)) for Euler bricks, (2) collects and ranks all near-misses from brute force and parametric searches, (3) computes statistical distribution of near-miss scores, (4) tests whether near-miss distribution is consistent with random or shows systematic avoidance of zero (evidence for non-existence). Produce a histogram plot of near-miss scores saved to results/near_miss_distribution.png.

items.description: Design and implement novel search strategy combining S3-symmetry reduction with elliptic curve methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/novel_search.py implementing: (1) S3-symmetry reduction to eliminate redundant permutations of edges per Sharipov's approach, (2) for promising Euler brick families, attempt to express the perfect cuboid condition as a point on an elliptic curve and search for rational points, (3) document the mathematical derivation in a docstring or accompanying novel_approach.md. The implementation must discover at least as many Euler bricks as the brute force approach in the same time budget and identify the 10 closest near-miss perfect cuboids found.

items.description: Implement constraint propagation and SAT/SMT-based feasibility checker
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/constraint_checker.py that: (1) encodes the perfect cuboid conditions as integer constraints, (2) uses modular arithmetic constraints from item_012 plus additional number-theoretic constraints (e.g., prime factor structure of space diagonal must be ≡1 mod 4), (3) implements constraint propagation to prune search space, (4) optionally interfaces with Z3 or a SAT solver if available to check feasibility of bounded instances. Document the constraint reduction factor achieved vs. unconstrained search.

items.description: Cross-domain concept exploration using ConceptEvolve probe and reframe
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve.py probe on 'integer solutions to coupled Pythagorean equations with shared variables' and concept_evolve.py reframe on the perfect cuboid problem. Analyze outputs for actionable algorithmic ideas. Document at least 2 novel algorithmic strategies suggested by the cross-domain analysis in novel_approach.md. If any strategy is implementable, create a prototype in src/experimental/.

items.description: Run systematic search reproducing known Euler brick catalogs
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute all search methods (brute force, modular sieve, parametric, novel) with edge bound >= 5000. Verify output against Helenius catalog of known Euler bricks. Report: (1) total Euler bricks found by each method, (2) any Euler bricks found by one method but missed by another, (3) perfect cuboid found: YES/NO. Save complete catalog to results/euler_brick_catalog.json.

items.description: Run comprehensive near-miss analysis across all search methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Aggregate near-miss data from all search methods. Produce results/near_miss_analysis.md containing: (1) table of top 20 closest near-miss perfect cuboids with edges, face diagonals, space diagonal, and gap, (2) comparison with known near-misses from the literature (e.g., (1887,2943,5247) near-miss), (3) statistical test of whether near-miss distribution favors non-existence. Include at least 2 publication-quality plots.

items.description: Compare search efficiency against prior published algorithms
items.acceptance_criteria: Benchmark all implemented algorithms and compare against published rates from the literature (Butler's algorithm, De Grey-Gibbs-Helm approach). Produce results/algorithm_comparison.md with: (1) table comparing candidates/second, filter efficiency, and coverage for each method, (2) speedup factor of modular sieve and novel search vs. baseline brute force, (3) estimate of how far each method could search given 1 hour, 1 day, and 1 week of compute time. Reference prior work from sources.bib.

items.description: Scaling analysis and computational feasibility study
items.acceptance_criteria: Run each search method at bounds 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000 (or as high as feasible within time budget). Produce results/scaling_analysis.md with: (1) log-log scaling plots for each method, (2) empirical complexity exponents (fit O(n^k) and report k), (3) extrapolation to published search frontiers (edge bound 10^10 to 10^13), (4) assessment of whether any novel method could realistically extend the search frontier. Include at least 2 scaling plots.

items.description: Ablation study on modular sieve prime set and constraint combinations
items.acceptance_criteria: Run modular sieve with varying numbers of primes (5, 10, 20, 50) and measure: (1) filtering rate for each configuration, (2) diminishing returns curve for adding more primes, (3) which individual primes provide the most filtering power, (4) interaction effects between constraint types (modular vs. parity vs. prime factor). Produce results/ablation_study.md with a table and at least 1 plot.

items.description: Write comprehensive research report
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce REPORT.md (minimum 2000 words) with sections: (1) Introduction and problem statement, (2) Literature review summary citing at least 10 papers from sources.bib, (3) Methods (all implemented algorithms with pseudocode), (4) Results (Euler bricks found, near-miss analysis, algorithm comparison), (5) Discussion (implications for perfect cuboid existence, comparison with prior computational results), (6) Conclusion. All claims must reference results from Phase 4 experiments.

items.description: Create summary tables of all results with comparison to prior work
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/summary_tables.md containing: (1) table of all Euler bricks found up to the search bound, (2) comparison table of our search methods vs. published methods from sources.bib (speed, coverage, novelty), (3) table of top near-misses compared against published near-misses, (4) table of modular sieve effectiveness by prime. All tables must be valid Markdown and reference specific sources.

items.description: Document limitations, open questions, and future research directions
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce LIMITATIONS.md documenting: (1) computational limits of our search (max bound achieved, time constraints), (2) mathematical limitations (what our methods cannot prove), (3) at least 3 concrete open questions arising from our analysis, (4) at least 3 specific future research directions with justification (e.g., GPU parallelization, connection to specific open conjectures, specific elliptic curve families to investigate), (5) honest assessment of whether the evidence favors existence or non-existence of a perfect cuboid.

items.description: Validate sources.bib completeness and create reproducibility package
items.acceptance_criteria: Verify sources.bib has at least 12 valid BibTeX entries and every citation in REPORT.md has a corresponding entry. Create requirements.txt (or equivalent) listing all Python dependencies. Create run_all.py that executes the complete experimental pipeline. Update README.md with project description, setup instructions, and summary of findings. All code in src/ and tests/ must be importable without errors.
